subject: Multivariate regression of non-coordinate data using procD.lm

messages.author: bc6140df818f0616
messages.subject: Multivariate regression of non-coordinate data using procD.lm
parts:
Hi all,

I'm trying to perform an allometric space analysis (PCA) based on the coefficients of a multivariate regression of my raw data (i.e. linear measurements). I have 24 shape variables and 1 size variable, and roughly 60 specimens from 9 species. Since I need the coefficients of my shape variables I ran the regression as size~shape, instead of shape~size (which is the basic structure recommended for procD.lm).

Now, when I try to do this for a specific species (n=14) I try the following:
(lm<-procD.lm(size~shape1+shape2+shape3...shape24,data = data[[1]]$`speciesname`,effect.type=c("F"),RRPP = TRUE,iter = 9999)

And I get the following error:

Error in array(x, c(length(x), 1L), if (!is.null(names(x))) list(names(x),  :
  'data' must be of a vector type, was 'NULL'

I'm guessing that it's because I have more shape variables than samples, so I tried running the same including fewer variables, and it works until I include n-1 shape variables.
I know of previous works that have used the same method and they were able to use this function to run a multivariate regression in this same scenario (i.e. fewer samples than shape variables). Can anyone point out my rookie mistake that I seem to miss?

Thanks in advanced!
Camilo

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Multivariate regression of non-coordinate data using procD.lm
parts:
Camillo,

The problem is likely caused by the fact that you have more shape variables than the rank of a matrix of shape variables.  If n = 14, then the maximum rank of a matrix of variables for describing the data of the 14 specimens is 13.  For example, if you were to do a PCA on what you are calling the shape variables, only 13 eigenvalues would be positive, meaning you only need 13 principal components to fully capture all the variation in your data.

The error happens because you started adding null dimensions to your linear model design matrix. Behind the scenes, procD.lm uses QR decomposition on design matrices to get the model rank (degrees of freedom).  After you added 13 variables, adding additional variables did not change the rank of the QR decomposition (0 degrees fo freedom added), so an error occurred when R tried to make a vector of nothing.

Another way to do this that might not spring an error is

fit <- procD.lm(size ~ shape, …)
fit$coefficients

where shape is the full matrix of 24 “shape” variables.  This might not cause an error, but you will only have 13 rows in your matrix of coefficients (not counting the intercept).

I do not fully understand the purpose of your analysis and I am not sure how you derived your size variable.  So a better question might be, “Why are you trying to predict size from shape?”  If this is an appropriate thing to do, you just have to realize that the shape variables are not independent of each other and should be limited in number to n - 1; i.e., the dimensions of your data space.

Cheers!
Mike
